Author: Pradeep Nandrajog Bench: Chief Justice  HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN BENCH AT  JAIPUR  S.B. Criminal Revision No. 1014 / 2002 Mohan Lal S/o Shri Balabux Ji, by caste: Mahajan, Resident of Village Baparda, Police Station: Nangal Rajavtan, District Dausa (Rajasthan)
 ----Petitioner  Versus The State of Rajasthan, through P.P.
 ----Respondent _____________________________________________________ For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Kailash Sharma

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN BENCH AT  JAIPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr. B.N. Sandu, Public Prosecutor _____________________________________________________ HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE Judgment 18/07/2017 1.

Convicted by the learned Magistrate vide order dated September 16, 1982 for having committed an offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the sample of milk being found to be below the specified standards, the petitioner was sentenced to undergo R.I. for one year and was fined  2500/-, in default to undergo S.I. for three months.
2. Appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed in default on February 7, 1989.
3. The police authorities could not locate the petitioner who was on bail before the Court of Sessions till September, 2002.
Unaware of the appeal being dismissed the petitioner sought bail from the Court of Sessions which dismissed the application seeking bail on September 12, 2002.
The petitioner was in Court (2 of 3) [CRLR-1014/2002] and was taken into custody.
He was granted bail by this Court in the instant revision petition on January 6, 2003 and was able to furnish the bail bonds and surety bonds 4 days later.
In this manner the petitioner has been in jail for four months.
4. Two options are available.
The first is to remand the matter to the learned District Judge who dismissed the appeal in default for the reason that for fault of Counsel the petitioner should not suffer.
The second is to decide the revision petition treating the same to be an appeal.
5. The record would show that the Food Inspector Laxminarain, PW1 lifted the milk sample at 6.30 am on July 7, 1976.
Sent to the public analyst report came that the milk sample lifted was adulterated on account of the fat and solids not being fat, being less than the prescribed standard.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has not been able to point out any infirmity in the lifting of the sample, its analysis or the authority of the Inspector who lifted the sample.
Thus I maintain the conviction.

7. Considering the time lag between the date when the sample was lifted which is July 7, 1976 and the decision in the petition, ends of justice would be met if while maintaining the conviction,
sentence imposed upon the petitioner is reduced from one year to six months with further direction as was issued by the Supreme Court in the decision reported as (2009) 8 SCR 175, State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The direction would be to the State Government to consider exercising its power under Section 433 Cr.P.C. and commute the balance sentence taking (3 of 3) [CRLR-1014/2002]
note of the fact that the offence was committed 41 years back.
The petitioner is an aged person.
He has already undergone imprisonment for four months.

8. I suspend the sentence for a period of four months within which the State Government would,
after taking cognizance of the present decision, decide request by the petitioner to commute the balance sentence.
The petitioner shall submit a representation to the competent authority within a week from today.
9. The revision petition is disposed of.

(PRADEEP NANDRAJOG),C.J.
